title: Afatinib monotherapy
scope_note: NCCP 00221a covers adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with an activating EGFR mutation who have not received an EGFR TKI. The separate licensed squamous-cancer indication after platinum treatment is not included in this NCCP regimen or its evidence card.
schedule_label: Daily oral treatment without a rest week
schedule_summary: The usual starting dose is 40 mg by mouth once daily, continuously without a planned rest week. Use the dose on your prescription. Treatment continues while it helps and side effects remain acceptable; any dose change is agreed with your team.
purpose: Afatinib blocks abnormal EGFR-family growth signals in selected lung cancers. Treatment aims to control advanced cancer and delay progression.
indication_text: NCCP 00221a covers adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with an activating EGFR mutation who have not received an EGFR TKI. The separate licensed squamous-cancer indication after platinum treatment is not included in this NCCP regimen or its evidence card.
administration_text: Take at the same time daily without food: leave at least 3 hours after food before the dose and wait at least 1 hour afterwards before eating. Swallow with water. If missed, take it the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip. Never double a dose or repeat a vomited dose. Ask pharmacy for the approved water-dispersion method if swallowing is difficult.
monitoring_summary: Confirm the activating EGFR test, previous treatments and prescription. Check blood count, kidneys and liver. A heart-pumping test (ECHO or MUGA) is used if clinically indicated. Review lungs, bowel, eyes, skin, all medicines and pregnancy precautions. NCCP specifies blood count, kidney and liver tests monthly. Heart-function tests are repeated if clinically indicated. Report diarrhoea and skin changes early, especially in the first weeks. Scans and cancer reviews follow your Consultant’s plan.

agents.name: Afatinib
agents.explanation: Afatinib is an irreversible EGFR-family tyrosine kinase inhibitor. It interrupts signals involved in cancer-cell growth; the tumour mutation test and treatment setting determine whether it is suitable.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea, rash, breathing changes and eye symptoms promptly.
risks: Rash, dry skin and nail changes
Rare serious skin reactions and bowel perforation

urgent_extra: Call urgently for new or worsening breathlessness, cough or fever; severe diarrhoea, inability to drink or much less urine; severe or persistent abdominal pain; blistering or peeling skin; or yellow skin/eyes. Eye pain, light sensitivity or blurred vision needs prompt assessment. Severe breathing difficulty, collapse or swelling of the tongue/throat needs emergency help. logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan
logistics.intro: The usual starting dose is 40 mg by mouth once daily, continuously without a planned rest week. Use the dose on your prescription. Treatment continues while it helps and side effects remain acceptable; any dose change is agreed with your team.

sections.title: Before starting
sections.text: Confirm the mutation, treatment setting, prescription, baseline tests, first review and emergency contact.

sections.title: Taking the tablets
sections.text: Take at the same time daily without food: leave at least 3 hours after food before the dose and wait at least 1 hour afterwards before eating. Swallow with water. If missed, take it the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip. Never double a dose or repeat a vomited dose. Ask pharmacy for the approved water-dispersion method if swallowing is difficult.

sections.title: Supplies and visits
sections.text: Arrange the next prescription before tablets run out. Keep your blood-test and clinic appointments. The oral regimen itself does not require an infusion line or pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held
sections.text: Ask why, what must recover and when review is due. Only the team authorises restarting or changing dose.

sections.title: At treatment change
sections.text: Agree ongoing symptom care, scans, contraception and follow-up.

evidence.title: Evidence for this treatment setting
evidence.intro: The mutation and prior treatment matter.
evidence.interpretation: In studies of selected EGFR-mutated advanced lung cancers, afatinib delayed cancer progression compared with cisplatin/pemetrexed. The overall survival comparison in that trial was not statistically significant. A separate comparison with gefitinib also did not show a statistically significant overall-survival difference. Ask how the study population and alternatives match your situation.
evidence.limitations: Study groups cannot predict your individual outcome or compare treatments from different trials.

teachback: Can you explain how to take your tablets, what to do after a missed or vomited dose, which tests are next and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: Discuss the aim of advanced cancer control, expected benefit and uncertainty, alternatives including not proceeding, bowel and skin effects, serious lung/liver problems, fertility and pregnancy, daily treatment, monitoring and your right to reconsider.

support.title: Diarrhoea and fluids
support.text: Keep prescribed anti-diarrhoea medicine available from the first dose. Start your agreed plan at the first loose stool, keep drinking if able and report symptoms early. Your team may advise continuing symptom medicine until loose stools have stopped for 12 hours. Severe diarrhoea, weakness or reduced urine needs urgent advice.

support.title: Skin, nails and mouth
support.text: Use the agreed EGFR-inhibitor skin-care and mouth-care plan. Emollients and sun protection may help; report rash, painful nails or mouth sores early. The team decides whether creams, antibiotics or other treatment are needed.

support.title: Nausea medicines
support.text: Afatinib has minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Routine infusion premedication is not required. Agree any as-needed anti-sickness medicine with the team, after checking interactions and your medical history.

support.title: Medicine interactions
support.text: Give pharmacy a list of all medicines, herbal products and supplements. Some P-gp inhibitors need separated dosing; strong inducers such as St John’s wort can reduce afatinib exposure. Ask for a written individual schedule before adding or changing medicines.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
support.text: Avoid pregnancy. Women who could become pregnant need adequate contraception during treatment and for at least 1 month after the final dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility and future pregnancy plans before starting.

questions.q: Is there a planned week off?
questions.a: No. These tablets are continuous daily treatment. A hold for side effects is a clinical decision.

questions.q: What if I miss a dose or vomit?
questions.a: Take at the same time daily without food: leave at least 3 hours after food before the dose and wait at least 1 hour afterwards before eating. Swallow with water. If missed, take it the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip. Never double a dose or repeat a vomited dose. Ask pharmacy for the approved water-dispersion method if swallowing is difficult.

questions.q: Can I adjust the dose myself?
questions.a: No. Keep the prescription and contact plan. Your team authorises every hold, restart or dose change.

questions.q: Do I need all the tests every day?
questions.a: No. Your team schedules tests and reviews. Contact them between appointments if symptoms occur.

chronology_notes.title: Duration
chronology_notes.text: No fixed course cap; continuation depends on benefit and tolerability.

chronology_notes.title: Dose decisions
chronology_notes.text: Afatinib dose changes are usually in 10 mg steps. Only the team may consider 50 mg after the initial 3 weeks if conditions are met; previous reductions rule out escalation. If 20 mg cannot be tolerated, a different treatment plan may be needed.
